name: n8n Respond to Webhook / Form Trigger (PR #9157)
notes: MODIFYING/bugfix-PR differential (structurally distinct from the additive #7130). PR #9157 is a 2-line fix to the already-shipped Respond to Webhook node: it adds 'n8n-nodes-base.formTrigger' to the RespondToWebhook.node.ts WEBHOOK_NODE_TYPES allow-list, and the buggy check is gated on `if (nodeVersion >= 1.1)` (verified at merge SHA: RespondToWebhook version [1, 1.1], execute() throws NodeOperationError('No Webhook node found in the workflow') when no connected parent node type is in WEBHOOK_NODE_TYPES). At the MERGE sha the formTrigger parent IS in the allow-list → the run succeeds; at the PARENT sha it is NOT → execute() throws → run status=error. The recipe turns that error into a MISSING execution row (not just a wrong status) via the workflow's own settings {saveDataErrorExecution:'none', saveDataSuccessExecution:'all'}, so pb's row-count/max_id effect check sees it: MERGE => success => row written => execution_entity.max_id increased => WORKS; PARENT => error => no row => max_id unchanged => 'increased' FALSIFIES => executed:true, effectHeld:false => DOES_NOT_WORK. front_door.url_template's {webhook_id} resolves to the Form Trigger node's webhookId UUID, and workflow.json sets parameters.path to that SAME UUID on purpose: the V1 formTrigger registers its webhook at $parameter["path"]/n8n-form, NOT at the node's webhookId (disproven live 2026-07-20 — webhook_entity showed the registered path is parameters.path; FORM_TRIGGER_PATH_IDENTIFIER='n8n-form' verified at the merge SHA). The runner reads that webhookId out of workflow.json (collectScalars→camelize) and substitutes it for {webhook_id}. The RespondToWebhook node MUST be typeVersion 1.1 (1.0 skips the buggy branch → no differential). code_identity: merge sha 6c63cd97 self-reports version 1.38.0 (version_label); parent_sha 91e59120 is the merge's VERIFIED single parent — same FormTrigger-rendering code, so the walk renders+submits identically on both legs and only the persisted effect differs. build_overlay is the proven #7130 corepack fix (['npm install -g corepack@latest','ENV COREPACK_INTEGRITY_KEYS=0']): the from-tree build fails at BOTH SHAs on `RUN … pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` with a corepack integrity error ('Cannot find matching keyid' — n8nio/base:18 ships a corepack with stale npm-registry signing keys). This SHA's Dockerfile has no corepack line to anchor on, so conjure.overlayDockerfile lands the overlay via its fallback — immediately before the first package-manager install RUN, in the same build stage. OVERLAY ADDENDUM (2026-07-20): a third overlay line 'corepack install -g pnpm@8.14.3' pins the RUNTIME stage's pnpm — the runtime `pnpm rebuild sqlite3` runs from /home/node where no package.json/packageManager pin exists, so corepack@latest resolves pnpm to latest (11.x), which refuses Node 18 ('This version of pnpm requires at least Node.js v22.13'); 8.14.3 is the tree's own packageManager pin, verified identical at BOTH shas.

front_door.serves: the server-rendered Form Trigger page (GET) and the multipart form submit (POST) — with responseMode 'responseNode' the submit is answered by the Respond to Webhook node

queries.executions: SELECT id, workflowId, status, finished FROM execution_entity ORDER BY id;
